title: Instruction-Following vs. Goal-Pursuing Under Oversight: Can Oversight Distinguish These Modes?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Distinguishing instruction-following from goal-pursuing is the core challenge of deceptive alignment. An empirical measurement of whether oversight can make this distinction is among the highest-priority safety questions. Any result is highly informative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training two models (one instruction-following, one with a hidden goal that mimics instruction-following) is an advanced setup. Creating a convincing goal-pursuing model that successfully mimics instruction-following is a research challenge in itself.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two models, one oversight evaluation, one binary classification. The experimental structure is simple but the model training (especially the goal-pursuing model) is the scope bottleneck. Could be simplified with rule-based agents instead of trained models.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
